proof:
# Three bisected source chords force a quantitative section-weight bound

This is an ordinary planar convex-body theorem. It applies to arbitrary convex bodies, with no polygon, symmetry or smoothness assumption. Three bisected chords do not imply that the body is centrally symmetric. The proof retains an actual opposite double-capture triangle when bounding a unique-capture sector.

## 1. Statement and normalization

Let K be a planar convex body, with 0 in its interior. Let nonzero normals v_1,v_2,v_3 span the plane and satisfy v_1+v_2+v_3=0. Assume that each of the three chords K intersect {v_i.x=0} is bisected at 0. Set

    k=|K|,
    q_i=|K intersect {v_i.x>=0}|,
    sigma_i=H_1(K intersect {v_i.x=0})/||v_i||,
    lambda_i=(1/sigma_i)/sum_j(1/sigma_j).

Suppose q_i<=c k for all i, where 0<c<1/2, and put epsilon=1-2c. Then

    min_i lambda_i >= 1/[1+sqrt(1+1/(2epsilon))].              (1)

If, additionally, the sorted cap volumes x<=y<=z obey

    x+y+z/4<=k,                                               (2)

then the stronger conclusion is

    min_i lambda_i >= 1/[1+sqrt(1+3c/(4epsilon))].             (3)

In particular, at c=128/279 the respective bounds are

    1/[1+sqrt(325/46)] > 2/9,
    1/[1+sqrt(119/23)] > 3/10 > 2/9.                          (4)

If the hypotheses have no body realizing them, the corresponding statement is simply vacuous; no existence of an extremizer is asserted.

The coordinate map x -> (v_1.x,v_2.x) has nonzero absolute determinant D. It scales all areas by D and all three normalized section lengths by the same factor D, since their scalar thresholds are unchanged. Thus it preserves cap fractions, (2), all lambda_i, and chord bisection. We may therefore use v_1=(1,0), v_2=(0,1), v_3=(-1,-1). Permuting the three normals is realized by the corresponding canonical linear maps with absolute determinant one.

Write the actual six ray endpoints as

    (A,0), (-A,0), (0,B), (0,-B), (R,-R), (-R,R),

where A,B,R>0. The normalized section lengths are sigma_1=2B, sigma_2=2A, sigma_3=2R. Relabel so that B>=max(A,R); then lambda_1 is a minimum. Put

    P=AR, S=A+R, L=BS+P, X=BS/P.

In particular BS-P>0 and

    lambda_1=1/(1+X).                                        (5)

## 2. A core area and an actual opposite sector

The six triangles joining 0 to successive ray endpoints lie in K by convexity and have disjoint interiors, since they occupy successive angular sectors. Their total area is

    L=AB+BR+AR.

Consequently k>=L. This argument does not presume that the six endpoints are strict vertices or that their convex hull is K.

Let

    Z_1=K intersect {y<0, x+y>0},
    D_1=K intersect {y>=0, x+y<=0}.

The first is the unique sector for the first cap; the second is the double-capture sector of the other two caps. The actual triangle with vertices 0,(-A,0),(-R,R) lies in D_1 and has area P/2. Hence

    |D_1|>=P/2.                                              (6)

Writing H_i={v_i.x>=0}, inclusion-exclusion gives

    q_2+q_3=k-|Z_1|+|D_1|.

All discrepancies on source lines have zero area. Thus the individual cap upper bounds imply

    epsilon k <= |Z_1|-|D_1| <= |Z_1|-P/2.                   (7)

Retaining the subtracted opposite-sector area is essential.

## 3. Exact unique-sector envelope

Use coordinates u=-y and v=x+y on Z_1, so u,v>0 and the coordinate map has determinant one. Joining an actual point (u+v,-u) to the endpoints (0,-B) and (0,B) and using the actual positive endpoints (R,-R) and (A,0) of the crossed source lines yields

    B u+(B-R)v<=BR,
    (B-A)u+B v<=BA.                                         (8)

For example, the first segment crosses x+y=0 at x=B(u+v)/(B+v), which cannot exceed R. The second crosses y=0 at x=B(u+v)/(B+u), which cannot exceed A. Both constraints therefore follow from actual segments in the same K.

Since B>=A,R, both row coefficients are nonnegative and the determinant has absolute value B(A+R)-AR=BS-P>0. The nonnegative-quadrant intersection is bounded. Its axis intercepts are (R,0) and (0,A): these endpoints are actual points of the transformed K sector, so the other inequality cannot shorten either intercept. Its remaining vertex is the intersection of the two oblique lines. The shoelace formula, or direct substitution of that intersection, gives its exact area

    E=[ARB(A+R)-B^2(A-R)^2]/[2(B(A+R)-AR)].                  (9)

If an intersection vertex coincides with an axis vertex, the same expression remains valid. This is also the substitution (a,b,rho,tau)=(R,A,B,B) in the independently audited two-segment envelope theorem `candidate 104bb1564dc1ac15`. Hence |Z_1|<=E. The actual axis feasibility ensures E is nonnegative; arbitrary positive radii not compatible with an actual K are never substituted.

The cancellation with (6) is exact:

    E-P/2 = [P^2-B^2(A-R)^2]/[2(BS-P)]
           <= P^2/[2(BS-P)].                               (10)

Combining (7), (10) and k>=L gives

    epsilon(BS+P) <= P^2/[2(BS-P)],
    2epsilon[(BS)^2-P^2] <= P^2.

Thus X^2<=1+1/(2epsilon). Equation (5) proves (1).

## 4. The joint cap profile supplies an additional area lower bound

Outside the three source lines, a point belongs to exactly one or two of the H_i. It cannot belong to all three because their normals sum to zero, and it cannot belong to none. Let D_total be the total area in the three double-capture sectors. Then

    q_1+q_2+q_3=k+D_total.                                  (11)

The three core triangles in those double sectors have total area L/2. Therefore D_total>=L/2. The sorted profile (2) is equivalently

    q_1+q_2+q_3-(3/4)max_i q_i <= k.

Using (11) and max q_i<=c k gives

    D_total<=(3/4)c k,
    k>=2L/(3c).                                             (12)

Use (12) instead of k>=L in (7)--(10). This gives

    [2epsilon/(3c)](BS+P) <= P^2/[2(BS-P)],
    X^2<=1+3c/(4epsilon).

Equation (5) proves (3). At c=128/279, epsilon=23/279. The roots become sqrt(325/46) and sqrt(119/23). The first is less than 7/2 because 1300<2254; the second is less than 7/3 because 1071<1127. These are exactly the strict comparisons in (4).

## 5. Scope

The source point is fixed and all quantities are ordinary planar cap volumes and section lengths. The proof covers every arbitrary convex body satisfying the three chord-bisection hypotheses. It does not assume that source 0 is the ordinary centroid or that the body is a simplex. It does not establish a general ordinary profile theorem when the chords are not bisected, nor identify the mixed critical weights 1/(sigma_K+2sigma_A) with the ordinary weights 1/sigma_K when sigma_A is positive. Those additional sections and their actual center displacements must be tracked separately.

The exact checker `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_bisected_chords_and_actual_needle_slab_recovery.py` independently clips a family of noncentrally symmetric bisected-chord triangles and their truncations, and checks the examples in the companion needle note. All 1,447 checks pass. These are example and algebra certificates; the arbitrary-body proof is Sections 1--4 above.
